dedupe_keys.name: m grct dynamic circular economy decision support model for recyclable waste management in low income municipalities with the data4 tool

description: M-GRCT is a circular economy decision support model for designing recyclable waste management systems in low-income municipalities, published in 2022 in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health by Vargas-Terranova and co-authors. It calculates two implementation scenarios and, unusually, integrates an assessment of sociocultural dynamics typical of such municipalities with the usual solid waste variables: carbon footprint from transporting recyclables, leachate and greenhouse gas generation, and growth in the number of associated recyclers and selective collection routes. Economic evaluation runs in a dynamic tool called DATA4, a macro workbook with two control panels programmed in Visual Basic and dashboards in Power BI. The authors applied it to the municipal solid waste system of Guateque, Colombia, over a ten-year horizon of rising recycling. The article is free under the Creative Commons Attribution licence; the DATA4 workbook is described in the paper, not published as a repository. Caveats: the model is demonstrated on one small municipality, depends on locally gathered sociocultural data, and the tool itself may need to be requested from the authors. Simulation uses: appraising recycling schemes and collection route expansion in small municipalities, comparing linear and circular scenarios on cost and emissions. Related records: the SWEET emissions tool (model-sweet-solid-waste-emissions-estimation-tool) estimates emissions for municipal waste systems and the Waste Wise Cities Tool (platform-un-habitat-waste-wise-cities-tool) supports collecting baseline data.
